comments.body:
@pcbeingused333 - How was the issue discovered? 
thanks for contributing

Found by reading the provider option converters side by side: the Mistral, Z.ai and other converters map `LlmOptions.maxTokens`, while `OllamaOptionsConverter` did not, so a configured limit was dropped for Ollama. It was not from a runtime bug report, and the change has only been checked with the unit tests in `OllamaOptionsConverterTest` (not against a live Ollama server). Happy to adjust if you'd rather map it differently.

(Drafted with the assistance of an AI coding agent.)

@igordayen, the [official Ollama parameter reference](https://docs.ollama.com/modelfile#valid-parameters-and-values) defines `num_predict` as “Maximum number of tokens to predict when generating text.” The [Spring AI Ollama reference](https://docs.spring.io/spring-ai/reference/api/chat/ollama-chat.html#_chat_properties) likewise describes `num-predict` as the generation token limit, separately from `num-ctx`, which sets the context window size. This is the conceptual mapping intended here: a positive `LlmOptions.maxTokens` value becomes the upper bound on generated tokens through `numPredict`, while an unset value leaves the provider default in place. The existing tests check this option conversion only; no live Ollama validation is claimed, and I can adjust the mapping in this PR if you prefer another interpretation.

This reply was prepared with the assistance of an AI coding agent.

> Looks fine to me. Thanks @pcbeingused333 for the contribution.

thanks @jorander 
@pcbeingused333 - please add comment as requested, thank you

@igordayen, done: I added a short code comment next to `.numPredict(options.maxTokens)` in `OllamaOptionsConverter` stating that Ollama's `num_predict` is the maximum number of tokens to generate (linking the Ollama parameter reference). Comment-only change, no behavior change.
